title: Interactive Analysis of Mills Ratios and Tail Thickness
text: millsratio package provides tools computing visualizing Mills ratios across different probability distributions. includes interactive dashboard exploring Mills ratios reveal fundamental differences distribution tails, particularly highlighting t(30) paradox distributions appear similar centrally diverge substantially tails. package implements extends concepts John D. Cook’s blog post Mills ratios.

title: Interactive Analysis of Mills Ratios and Tail Thickness
text: t(30) distribution often considered “practically normal” many applications. However: - Central region: Nearly indistinguishable normal - Tail region: Substantially different Mills ratios - Implication: Risk models based normality assumptions may severely underestimate tail probabilities

title: Interactive Analysis of Mills Ratios and Tail Thickness
code:
# Verify that normal has decreasing Mills ratio (thin tails) x <- seq(1, 5, by = 0.5) m <- mills_ratio_normal(x) cat("Normal Mills ratio decreasing:", all(diff(m) < 0), "
")  # Verify that t(3) has increasing Mills ratio (fat tails) m_t <- mills_ratio_t(x, df = 3) cat("t(3) Mills ratio increasing:", all(diff(m_t) > 0), "
")  # Verify exponential has constant Mills ratio m_exp <- mills_ratio_exp(x) cat("Exponential Mills ratio constant:", all(abs(diff(m_exp)) < 1e-10), "
")

code: # Analyze normal distribution hazard hazard_properties("normal") #> $distribution #> [1] "normal" #>  #> $behavior #> [1] "Increasing (IFR - Increasing Failure Rate)" #>  #> $asymptotic_behavior #> [1] "h(x) ~ x as x -> Inf" #>  #> $interpretation #> [1] "Aging effect - failure rate increases with x" #>   # Compare properties across distributions library(purrr) list(   normal = hazard_properties("normal"),   t30 = hazard_properties("t", df = 30),   exponential = hazard_properties("exponential") ) %>%   map_df(~ as.data.frame(.x), .id = "distribution") #>   distribution                                   behavior #> 1       normal Increasing (IFR - Increasing Failure Rate) #> 2          t30                              Non-monotonic #> 3  exponential     Constant (CFR - Constant Failure Rate) #>          asymptotic_behavior                                  interpretation #> 1       h(x) ~ x as x -> Inf    Aging effect - failure rate increases with x #> 2 h(x) ~ 31/30/x as x -> Inf Heavy tails - lower hazard than normal in tails #> 3            h(x) = constant              Memoryless - constant failure rate
